questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being an Australian who grew up in Denmark, I had a personal connection to the country that I wanted to explore during my exchange. However, going to the University of Melbourne was also important to me, as I had heard that the school was a great place to study. The courses offered were exciting, and I could apply to a lot of different courses as a student of Anthropology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The information was fairly easy to find. Most of the info needed was provided by KU during information sessions, mails and links to info pages. UniMelb also had a good step-by-step guide on how to get my exchange in order - how to apply for courses, student cards and such. Unimelb also held an orientation session for exchange students at the beginning of the semester.

I did have to do a bit of research into how to navigate the course catalogue. It was a bit tricky figuring out what courses were available to me, and which I was eligible for, as well as how to submit them for approval from KU. I feel there could be more information on that part of the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved help from UniMelb's student service because of some confusion about getting my vaccination certificate certified. The rules were changing, so there was mixed information about what to do. I was also in touch with other Danish exchange students during the first weeks, and we helped each other out with questions and problems in a groupchat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
There were student dorms available through the University of Melbourne. I applied to the cheapest of the dorms, Lisa Bellear House. I payed $350/week in rent, and I know the rent is going up next year.
In order to live in the dorms, you sign a lease that lasts whole semester, and the lease can only be broken early under special circumstances. It's something to keep in mind if you're thinking about renting a dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The cooking facilities depend on the room. I had a stove top with two burners and a microwave, because I lived in a twin room. Bigger rooms have ovens. There was also a common kitchen with a couple of ovens and stoves available for cooking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
In my opinion, on-campus housing is expensive for what it is, but Melbourne is an expensive city. I know that some of my friends found cheaper places to rent, but rent prices are very high in Melbourne in general. I chose to apply for housing because I had the budget for it, and I wanted to live close to campus. I also wanted to have my housing situation sorted upon arrival in the unfamiliar city.

On the upside, the dorm is a fun community of students from all over the place, and I've made some great friends here. The dorm also hosts a number of events every week which gives you an opportunity to get to know everyone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot to keep track of when registering at UniMelb, but the university provides guides on how to register courses. The timetable application is tricky to navigate, but I managed to register for my desired class times.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You have to accept your letter of offer, then complete an administrative enrolment. After your enrollment is confirmed, you can enroll in your subjects. Remember to get your subjects approved by KU so you can transfer the course credits at the end of your stay!
Create your timetable before the semester starts as well (there's a guide on the page I've linked below). The timetable tool can be a bit tricky to use - I had to spend some time on it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UniMelb has a student service called Stop-1. The exchange coordinator from KU was also able to answer some questions for me intitally.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted successfully, and the timetable I wanted was approved as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
This page was very helpful for me:
https://students.unimelb.edu.au/new-students/get-started/saex
I followed the steps listed on the page to register for courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were challenging, but they were at an appropriate level for me. I studied on my 5th semester, and took two Level 2 BA subjects and two Level 3 BA subjects. I could definitely tell that the Level 3 subjects were more challenging, but I also got a lot out of them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching was very engaging, and it was interesting studying with a different group of students for each course. At KU I had studied only with other antropology students during the obligatory courses. I liked getting some different perspectives on the courses.
The biggest difference I think is the way the workload is distributed. You're working on assessments throughout the semester, as opposed to KU, where only the final exam is graded. This puts a lot more pressure on mid-semester assignments, and it took me a while to find a rhythm with the workload that worked for me. Checking when all the assessments are due and planning when you're going to work on them is definitely important at UniMelb if you want to avoid doing it all last minute (like me).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Indigenous Cultures and Knowledges (UNIB20022_2022_SM2)
Life Writing (CWRI30013_2022_SM2)
Short Fiction (CWRI20002_2022_SM2)
Trans Studies: Cultures and Communities (GEND30007_2022_SM2)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed all my courses a lot, but my favourites were Life Writing and Trans Studies. They were relevant to my personal interests, but I think they would be beneficial to anthropology students generally.
Life Writing is a non-fiction writing class with a focus on biography. It taught me a lot about writing about my own and other peoples' lives, and I found the in-class discussions very engaging.
Trans Studies is a relatively recent field of study that focuses on transgender and genderqueer experience. The topics covered in class were varied and cover the complexity of trans experiences.

To anthropology students I recommend "Indigenous Cultures and Knowledges." It's a masterclass series taught by experts in each field, and it covers many different fields of study concerning Indigenous Australian culture and knowledge. I found the class challenging, as it covers a very broad field of interest, but illuminating as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rent was a lot more expensive than I'd expected. Also fees for banking, such as currency conversion fees whenever you pay for sometthing or transfer money into a foreign account.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee in Melbourne is cheaper than in Copenhagen, as well as some other café foods and beverages. In general restaurant foods and groceries cost about the same. The rent is what really drives up the cost of living.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any clubs, but I participate in events at my dorm.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of things! There's a lot more variety than the clubs at KU. During the orientation week they hand out guides to all the clubs you can participate in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any clubs, sorry! Make sure to grab a coffee with friends around the campus, though. There are a lot of coffee shops on campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is a vibrant city with tons to do. I loved the botanical gardens, museums and cafés in the center of town. The food is also excellent, but not cheap. Make sure to see some live music while you're here!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found the culture quite easy to adjust to, as I come from Australia and have some friends here. Meeting other exchange students who were also new to the culture was very helpful in getting comfortable in Melbourne.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get to know your classmates, participate in clubs, sports, whatever you find interesting! You're sure to find likeminded people. I made a lot of great friends in my classes and at my dorm.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure I found the culture challenging. The first few months were hard, as I had to adjust to the clock and the seasons, and form new routines. After I had gotten settled in the city I had a great time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the people and the nature. Australia is just a beautiful place, and there are always more things to see.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Keep your budget in mind - Melbourne is not a cheap city. The rent especially brings up the cost of living.
2. The courses at the University of Melbourne can be challenging depending on courses you decide on, but they are rewarding if you're prepared to put in the work.
3. Get in touch with other students! I've met so many amazing people, both Australians and exchange students. They were what made my experience amazing!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people from all over the world, living in and exploring a whole new city, and the course at UniMelb.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness and adjusting the culture at first, as well as some issues with a roommate that I had to sort out with my dorm.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
